bug_semantics: Missing authorization on the logged-in WordPress AJAX action tec_qr_code_modal. QR_Code::render_modal() loads an arbitrary post via request post_id and returns its title plus generated QR images without current_user_can('edit_post') (and, until the patch, without check_ajax_referer). wp_ajax_tec_qr_code_modal is registered (not nopriv), so any authenticated Subscriber can invoke admin-ajax.php and disclose draft event names and QR codes. CWE-862. Feature shipped in 6.12.0; advisory range is all versions through 6.15.9; patched in 6.15.10.
flaw_origin: d26394e9c59cf1ab5450e5c8811be5ace9f95734 ('QR modal in events table', 2025-03-31) first created src/Events/QR/QR_Code.php and first registered add_action('wp_ajax_tec_qr_code_modal', [QR_Code, 'render_modal']). The original handler (lines 89–136) called get_post(tec_get_request_var('post_id')), gated only on tribe_is_event(), then emitted get_the_title($post) and a QR image. No capability check and no nonce verification were ever present until the 6.15.10 security fix. Later QR-feature commits expanded post types and image generation but did not introduce the missing-auth; blame at 6.15.9 still attributes the function signature and get_post line to that first write.
